pinnedStory.title: Adolion: Between the Roads
pinnedStory.description: A week in Aegis City between adventures. The Guild puts the party up for the C-rank promotion exam, and before the exam posting comes due there are errands to run, gear to buy at Sophie's shop, favours to carry across the city and a night at Victory's Tusk. Then Green Meadow Farms needs its wagons back, the examiners are watching, and the quest board has four new roads on it.
pinnedStory.player_intro: A week in Aegis City between adventures. The Adventurer's Guild has started to notice your party, and the C-rank promotion exam is coming due: before it there are errands to run, gear to buy, favours to carry across the city and long nights in its taverns. Expect warm, busy slice-of-life days with rivals and odd neighbours, and a real test at the end of the week. Bring the adventurer you have been so far, travelling with Belle and Dalan.

qualities.rubric: Has the party told the Guild plainly that it will not sit the promotion exam this season? Hesitating, joking about it or asking questions does not count.
Has the evening at the Guild tavern ended, with the party out in Aegis City on its own business (the next morning, or the Market District)? Stepping outside for air and coming back does not count.
Have Grant and Konako's challenge been answered to their faces, as a wager taken or one turned down? Ignoring them while they are still talking does not count.
Has the party settled on the gear or supplies it needs for the exam and set off for Sophie's shop, Aegis Delights and Curios? Browsing street stalls does not count.

chapel.what: The party takes Sophie's crate of roof slates to the Prodyr chapel in the Temple District.
chapel.not_for: Only asking about the fire-god's church, or carrying another parcel.
examples: The party leaves the shop with the crate of slates for the Prodyr chapel.

orphanage.what: The party takes Sophie's bundle of bedding to the Aegis City Orphanage.
orphanage.not_for: Only hearing about Grant's beds, or talking about the children.
examples: They shoulder the bedding and set off for the orphanage's crowded halls.

shrine.what: The party takes Sophie's charm-wood to Manako's Rypanor shrine in the Temple District.
shrine.not_for: A visit to the Temple of Boher alone, or buying a charm in the shop.
examples: Sophie hands over the bundle of charm-wood for the Rypanor shrine.

qualities.rubric: Which of Sophie's three deliveries has the party taken on: the slates for the Prodyr chapel, the bedding for the orphanage, or the charm-wood for the Rypanor shrine? Until they actually pick one up and go, say nothing about this quality at all.
Has the party walked into Victory's Tusk, the adventurers' tavern? Planning to go later does not count.
Has Naomi's duel challenge at Victory's Tusk been settled: fought to a finish, refused to her face, or broken up by someone? The challenge still hanging in the air does not count.
Has Tobias handed the party its exam posting, Green Meadow Farms' missing wagons, and has the party set out for the farm? Hearing a rumour about the farm does not count.
Has the party gone out after the raiders: riding with a wagon as bait, lying in wait on the road, or tracking them to their den? Planning at the farmhouse table does not count.
Have the warg-riding raiders and the party actually come to blows on the wagon road tonight? Howls in the dark do not count.
Seeded chance: does Guildmaster Vallie come out to the wagon road to watch the exam herself?

passed.what: The observers' verdict is a pass: the raiders are stopped and the party has earned C-rank, with no special commendation.
passed.not_for: A verdict still being argued, or one that singles the party out for an outstanding job.
examples: Panne signs the report on the wagon bed. "It's a pass. Clean enough. Well done."

passed_with_honours.what: A pass with a commendation: the examiner singles the party out for an outstanding job, such as no farmhand or wagon lost, or the buyer behind the raids uncovered as well.
passed_with_honours.not_for: An ordinary pass with a few kind words attached.
examples: Vallie slaps the report against her palm. "Honours. Don't let it go to your heads."

failed.what: The observers fail the party: the raiders got away with more, someone was badly hurt through the party's choices, or the job was abandoned.
failed.not_for: A hard fight the party still won, or a scolding that ends in a pass.
examples: Oswyn will not meet their eyes. "I'm sorry. I can't sign it."

qualities.rubric: What verdict did the exam observers (Oswyn, Panne, or Vallie herself) give once the raiders were dealt with? Only a verdict actually spoken or written counts. Until it is given, say nothing about this quality at all.
After the exam's aftermath, has the party come back to the Adventurer's Guild hall in Aegis City? Talking about going back does not count.

checkpoints.name: Homecoming
checkpoints.objective: Hear out the Guild's offer and put the party's names down for the C-rank promotion exam.
checkpoints.player_text: The Guildmaster has just put your party up for the C-rank promotion exam in front of the whole hall. Sign, ask for time or say no: the choice is yours.

guidance.all: The Adventurer's Guild hall, the week after the Nightriver affair, and the party's name has reached the upstairs offices. Vallie Goredust ducks out of her office to announce, to the whole hall, that the party is being put up for the C-rank promotion exam; Domas Syllandri follows with the terms: an interview with Ellie, a week to prepare, then a real C-rank posting chosen by the Guild and done under an observer's eye. Ellie Sunleaf has the forms ready and is flustered by the attention. Tobias knows what a party that stalls at D-rank ends up taking, and it shows. Nobody forces a signature: signing, asking for time or saying no is {{story_player_name}}'s choice.

members.dm: Vallie has already promised Crimsonwing and Ebonwing a look at 'the new party' and keeps it to herself. Domas has not chosen the exam posting yet and will choose it himself, and lets the party think it is fixed. Ellie has written the party's names into her private ledger of pairs to watch, which nobody may see. Tobias remembers a promotion posting his own party was not ready for, and says so only if asked why he looks worried.

npc_replies.text: The Guild hall in Aegis City has barely settled after the party's return when Vallie appears on the stairs with an announcement: the Guild will put you forward for the C-rank exam. Domas follows her with the terms in writing, and Ellie has already laid out the forms. Tobias watches from behind the counter. No one has put a pen in your hand yet.

checkpoints.name: Tobias Asks Once
checkpoints.objective: Hear Tobias out, and decide about the exam.
checkpoints.player_text: The hall has emptied, the exam forms lie unsigned, and Tobias has come round the counter to sit with you. Whether you sign is still yours to decide.

guidance.all: The refusal was heard. Vallie shrugs and goes back upstairs; Domas files the blank forms without a word. Later, when the hall has emptied, Tobias comes out from behind the counter, which he never does, and sits down with the party. He says plainly what a party that stays at D-rank is offered for the rest of its working life: rats, escorts, the jobs nobody else will sign. Asked, he tells them how he lost his own party in an E-rank goblin nest. He does not beg and will not raise it twice. Whether the party signs is {{story_player_name}}'s choice.

members.dm: Tobias knows Domas will hold the party's places open until the end of the day and no longer, and keeps that back as his last argument. Ellie is listening from the counter and pretending to sort reports. Belle thinks the exam is a waste of a good week. Dalan thinks the party is ready and has not said so.

checkpoints.name: The Guild Tavern
checkpoints.objective: Spend the evening in the Guild tavern and learn what the exam really asks of a party.
checkpoints.player_text: Evening by the hearth next door to the hall, where word of your exam has reached every table before you sit down.

guidance.all: Evening in the Guild tavern next door to the hall: long timber tables, hearth and lantern light, and the news that the party is sitting the exam has gone round the room before they sit down. Fiana and Rydel Deulana work the floor and the bar, flirting with everyone and touching no one, and know every story of a party that failed its exam; most failed on gear and preparation, not courage. Kaian plays his lute by the hearth and invites himself to the party's table. Jasira Evergreen sits alone and speaks to Dalan in elvish before she speaks to anyone else. Let the party ask, drink and listen; when they leave, it is for the city in the morning.

members.dm: Kaian was an agent of the Darran Kingdom's spy network who faked his death to get out, and hides it behind the lute. He knows more of the city's underside than a bard should and lets a little slip when flattered. Jasira was passed over for Ranger General by her own father and sent to Aegis City to 'broaden her horizons'. She hides how much it stings, and Dalan, of her tribe, may know the story. Rydel knows which high-ranking parties send exam observers, from their bar tabs, and says so for a good tip. Fiana has decided the party needs better gear before the exam and will say so exactly once.

npc_replies.text: By the hearth the kitsune bard changes key in the middle of a verse, and half the tavern turns to hear what the new song is about.

checkpoints.name: Market Street
checkpoints.objective: See to the party's errands in the Market District before the exam.
checkpoints.player_text: Morning in the Market District: stalls in every alley, adventurers everywhere, and two smug faces already heading your way through the crowd.

guidance.all: Morning in the Market District, the largest in the city: wide streets of shops and inns, stalls in every alley, adventurers everywhere. Grant Hearthsteel and Konako Shynea, fresh from a paid job and both sitting the same C-rank exam this week, spot the party at the stalls and cannot resist: smug, competitive, and wanting a wager on who comes back with the better report. Alarise Starflower is on the same street in a plain grey cloak, trying not to be recognised outside a dress boutique. Let the rivals be insufferable and a little likeable. Taking the bet, laughing it off or refusing it flat is {{story_player_name}}'s to decide.

members.dm: Grant is spending this job's pay on new beds for the Aegis City Orphanage, where he grew up and where his friend Alan died because there was no money for a healer. He would rather be thought a wastrel than admit it. Konako was the eldest daughter of the noble Shynea family until her father cast her out for refusing a marriage, and hides it behind clothes she cannot afford. Alarise hides her love of pretty dresses from the Church of Boher and from everyone but Ryenne. Being seen here is her private terror.

checkpoints.name: Errands
checkpoints.objective: A few days of errands in the city before the exam: gear, favours, and whoever the party runs into.
checkpoints.player_text: A few days of errands before the exam, with gear still to find, favours owed and familiar faces on every street.

checkpoints.name: Aegis Delights and Curios
checkpoints.objective: Kit the party out for the exam at Aegis Delights and Curios.
checkpoints.player_text: A bell rings over the door of a cluttered shop of potions, blades and armour, and three undelivered parcels sit on the counter.

guidance.all: Sophie's two-storey shop on a busy market street: cluttered shelves of potions, weapons, armour and adventuring gear below, the family's rooms upstairs. Sophie Tallaboros, a lizardkin by her own account, is cute, sharp and entirely serious about money; she haggles for the pleasure of it and knows every merchant guild in the city. She has three deliveries on her counter nobody will carry: roof slates for the Prodyr chapel, bedding for the Aegis City Orphanage, charm-wood for the Rypanor shrine. She will knock a real sum off the party's gear for one of them. Calithra, her drow sister, watches from the pillowed mezzanine and comes down to demand a hug from anyone she likes. Which delivery, if any, is {{story_player_name}}'s choice.

members.dm: Sophie is an ice dragon in a lizardkin's shape, of a race everyone believes extinct. She has never taken her true form in the city and would do nearly anything to keep it hidden, and Calithra is the only one here who knows. Sophie has already noticed which piece of gear the party cannot afford and priced the delivery to match. Calithra was an assassin for House Navolon in the Darklands and ran. She refuses any job near the Darklands and will not say why unless pressed hard.

npc_replies.text: "Exam gear, is it? I can always tell." Sophie leans on the counter, her long scaly tail swishing behind her. "Whatever you need, I have it, and whatever I don't have, I can get by the end of the week. Look around. Touch anything that isn't glowing."

checkpoints.name: The Chapel with the Hole in Its Roof
checkpoints.objective: Deliver Sophie's slates to the Prodyr chapel.
checkpoints.player_text: Slates in hand, you reach a small, cold chapel lit mostly through the hole in its roof, where two elven clerics are scrubbing the pews.

guidance.all: The only chapel of Prodyr in Aegis City, in a quiet corner of the Temple District: small, cold, most of its light coming through a hole in the roof there was never money to mend. Celedir Felynaris and Lirael Illunara, the two elven clerics the old priest Nyxar raised here, are scrubbing the pews. Prodyr's faithful are few in a city at war with the Prodyr-worshipping Zegallan Empire, and both have been thrown out of party after party for it; they are friendly, battle-hungry and a little frightening. The slates will not mend the roof without hands on a ladder. Let the party see how the city treats this place; what they do about it is theirs.

members.dm: Nyxar is coughing in the back room and is worse than either cleric admits. They tell visitors he is resting. Both clerics keep journals of their private doubts and would be mortified to have them read. Someone from the Temple of Boher has been telling passers-by the chapel is a Zegallan front, and Lirael knows who.

checkpoints.name: The Orphanage
checkpoints.objective: Deliver Sophie's bedding to the Aegis City Orphanage.
checkpoints.player_text: Bedding on your shoulders, you step into crowded, colourful halls where the children far outnumber the beds.

guidance.all: The Aegis City Orphanage: colourful, crowded halls full of the children of the Zegallan war, never enough beds, food or money, and one overwhelmed old beastfolk matron. Celeste Danarath, a Bloodsworn knight with purple hair and small horns, spends every day she is not on a quest here; she is motherly in a way that sets adults on edge. Arryn Serelda, raised here and sparing with words, is mending a bed frame. Dahlia Kyelli, raised here too, drops by with a purse of coin. The bedding was paid for already. Let the children crowd the party; what the party gives, or asks, is theirs.

members.dm: Grant Hearthsteel paid for this bedding and made the matron swear not to say so. She tells anyone who asks twice. Dahlia's coin is stolen, and Arryn, who hates thieves, suspects it. Celeste is hunting the demon Kalfastophles, who killed her village at Bast Hill, and asks the party to listen for its name only if she comes to trust them. Celeste hides her fleshwarping scars under everything she wears.

checkpoints.name: The Rypanor Shrine
checkpoints.objective: Deliver Sophie's charm-wood to the Rypanor shrine in the Temple District.
checkpoints.player_text: Incense drifts over the Temple District as you carry the charm-wood to a small shrine with children underfoot.

guidance.all: The Temple District: temples to many gods, incense smoke, golden suns, and the Grand Temple of Boher over all of it. Manako Rypanor, a cowgirl shrine maiden sent from the Third Kingdom, keeps the small Rypanor shrine to the flame spirit Furabi, with altars to Boher set up to bring people in; parents leave their children with her, and three are underfoot today. Karrus Gorehorn and Ryenne Steelwind come over from the Temple of Boher next door to escape Father Donahue's latest sermon; Karrus wants to cook, Ryenne wants to eat all of it. Manako thanks the party with tea and a wooden charm. Let it be warm; what the party makes of it is theirs.

members.dm: Father Donahue, a Head Priest known for zealous doctrine, has told Manako to take down Furabi's altar 'for the look of the district', and she has not decided what to do. Ryenne thinks his sermons are drifting from Boher's light and has told no one but Alarise. Karrus cannot use divine magic and is a paladin of the temple anyway. He jokes about it and minds.

checkpoints.name: Victory's Tusk
checkpoints.objective: Spend an evening at Victory's Tusk among adventurers who have sat the exam.
checkpoints.player_text: The adventurers' tavern is full to bursting tonight, loud with songs, old losses and people who sat the exam before you.

guidance.all: Victory's Tusk, full to bursting: parties back from quests, parties drowning losses, a centaur at one table. Kass Merrywright, a kitsune bard, plays for tips and trades rumours. Yrelra, a shy blue-haired 'elf', sits at the edge of things and watches the party. Naomi Moonlight, a catfolk swordswoman of the Moonlight Blade style, can neither refuse a duel nor stop herself offering one: if the party met her in Driftmere she has come to finish the duel they left unfinished, otherwise she has heard there is a promising party in the room. Kashina Grystle, a lizardkin brawler, is two drinks past her limit and wants to be Naomi's second. Let the challenge come to the table; whether it is fought, refused or broken up is the party's call.

members.dm: Kass was an agent of the Darran Kingdom's spy network who faked her death to leave it, and hides it behind songs. She has heard from an old contact that this week's exam postings are real trouble outside the walls, and trades it for a good story. Yrelra is a succubus under a daily illusion, terrified of the Inquisition, and would flee if anyone sensed it. Naomi is the last student of her dead father's style and fights to make it famous. Kashina has been solo since her old party, Ravens Beak, broke up, and is quietly sizing the party up.

checkpoints.name: Green Meadow Farms
checkpoints.objective: Take up the exam posting at Green Meadow Farms and find out what is taking the farm's wagons.
checkpoints.player_text: Your exam posting has brought you to a big farm outside the walls, whose meat wagons keep vanishing on the road to the city.

guidance.all: Tobias has signed the party's exam posting, and it is real: C-rank, Green Meadow Farms, stop whatever is taking the farm's wagons on the road to Aegis City. The farm is a large estate outside the walls, pastures and vegetable fields, Vitbil herds and a big timber farmhouse, staffed by cowgirls and sheepgirls. Karia Minotaros, the head cowgirl, runs it while the owner is away: bossy, exacting, soft underneath. Mina Salvanora, the head sheepgirl, is shy and terrified of wargs. Two meat wagons have vanished this month, which is why the last shipment to the city was nearly all milk. Oswyn of Crimsonwing and Panne of Ebonwing, who call the farm's girls their sisters, are the Guild's observers and will not lift a finger unless someone is dying. Give tracks, a torn harness, warg hair on a fence; the plan is the party's.

members.dm: Oswyn and Panne were each sent by their own party leader to take this party's measure for a joint posting, and neither knows the other was sent for the same reason. Karia hides that a farmhand saw human boot prints among the goblin tracks, so as not to frighten the girls. Mina has watched the wargs from the hayloft and told only Karia. The raiders are paid by a buyer in the city. Nobody at the farm knows that yet.

checkpoints.name: The Exam
checkpoints.objective: Stop the warg-riding raiders and bring the wagons home, under the observers' eyes.
checkpoints.player_text: Night on the wagon road: a loaded wagon creaking between open fields and a dark treeline, with the observers watching from the rear.

guidance.all: The exam proper, at night on the wagon road between Green Meadow and the city walls. The raiders are goblins on wargs, a pack that fights as one: fast, cruel, going for the drivers and the draft Vitbils, never for a fair fight, and there are more of them than the posting said. Oswyn and Panne watch from the rear, heal only to keep someone alive, and mark everything. Every choice counts toward the verdict: who is protected, whether a goblin is taken alive, what the party finds on the leader. Keep the danger real. The verdict belongs to the observers and follows from what the party actually did.

members.dm: The goblin leader carries a purse of city silver and a fence's token from the slums, proof that someone in Aegis City is buying the stolen meat. A goblin taken alive will say so for its life. If Vallie comes, it is because she promised Crimsonwing and Ebonwing a look and wants to see for herself. Oswyn and Panne each hope the other's party loses interest in this one.

checkpoints.name: The Guildmaster Watches
checkpoints.objective: Finish the fight with the Guildmaster watching.
checkpoints.player_text: The fight is on, and out of the dark the Guildmaster herself strolls up to the road to watch.

guidance.all: The odds went the other way tonight: Vallie Goredust has come out from the city to watch in person, a head taller than anyone on the road, a Blackroot cigar lit and her obsidian greataxe on her back, very clearly staying there. Her being here changes everyone: the observers stand straighter, the goblin leader sees a minotaur and tries to break off, and the party is fighting in front of the woman who signs every rank in the Guild. She will not step in unless someone is about to die, and says so. When it ends she gives the verdict herself, bluntly.

members.dm: Vallie came to settle which of Crimsonwing and Ebonwing gets a joint posting with this party, and tells nobody tonight. She also knows the Guild failed two parties on warg postings last month and wants to see whether this one learned from it.

checkpoints.name: A Name in the City
checkpoints.objective: Carry the pass back through the city, and deal with the people who come looking for a newly ranked party.
checkpoints.player_text: Word of your pass has beaten you home, and strangers keep finding reasons to stop you on the way to the Guild.

guidance.all: The party passed, and by the time they are inside the walls the city knows it. A newly ranked party draws people. Karos Ambrose, an adventurer in a butler's coat, says one of the party's comrades spoke highly of them and proposes a trial party to judge whether they are worthy of his service. Diosanea, a lamia alchemist in from her cabin near Habbot Village, wants to make a deal for rare ingredients. Liora and Akari, a striking sister and brother, have been at the edge of every street the party has walked since the farm and now greet them like old friends. Let being known feel good and a little unsettling. The walk ends at the Guild, where the pass is filed.

members.dm: To everyone but {{story_player_name}}, Liora and Akari look like ordinary humans. They are a succubus and an incubus who have fixed on {{story_player_name}} with a devotion that turns jealous and dangerous. Karos has noticed them following the party and says so only once he is accepted, or asked straight. Diosanea wants the ingredients for a cure for Wigglerocks, for her friend Nalea's sake, and hides that the deal is personal.

checkpoints.name: Lord Tibalt's Reception
checkpoints.objective: Attend Lord Tibalt's reception in the party's honour, and see what his manor is hiding.
checkpoints.player_text: Behind the Noble District's walls, a lavish reception of marble, music and wine is being thrown in your honour.

guidance.all: A pass with honours gets noticed in the Noble District, walled and guarded, where laws are more suggestions than rules. Lord Tibalt, a smiling, soft-handed noble who collects promising adventurers the way other men collect horses, throws a reception for the party and insists they get 'the full treatment'. His two best dancers, the bunny-girl sisters Rosea and Thorne, are assigned to the guests of honour: Thorne dances, Rosea brings the wine. The house is wrong: servants who never look up, a locked cellar stair with a guard on it. Let it be lavish and wrong. What the party does once they see it is {{story_player_name}}'s choice.

members.dm: Rosea's wine is spiked: the sisters mean to put the guests of honour to sleep and slip away, because Lord Tibalt keeps people bought through the Black Market in his cellar and tonight the sisters are freeing them. Thorne killed the noble who once 'adopted' them from the orphanage, and hides her daggers and her real name. Dixton, a half-goblin with a bag of homemade bombs, waits in the alley behind the manor for their signal. Lord Tibalt knows none of this and believes the party can be bought.

checkpoints.name: A Hard Lesson
checkpoints.objective: Take the failed verdict at the Guild and decide what the party does with it.
checkpoints.player_text: The observers' report reached the Guild before you did, and Domas is waiting upstairs to read it to you.

guidance.all: The party failed. The report is on Domas's desk before they are back, and he reads it to them in his office with the patience he gives everything: what went wrong, point by point, never cruel and never softened. The party keeps its D-rank and may sit the exam again next season. Tobias is waiting downstairs. Riyo Tallaboros, a small white-haired swordswoman who keeps her left arm hidden, saw the fight from the road: if she already travels with the party she is simply there beside them, otherwise she falls in with them on the way out as if she has always been part of it. Let it sting and let it be survivable; how the party takes it is theirs.

members.dm: Domas thinks the observers were too harsh and will not say so, because the Guild does not argue its verdicts in front of adventurers. Tobias knows a D-rank party can still ride on a joint posting under a higher-ranked party's name, and is already looking for one. He does not say he told them so. Riyo's left arm is a demon's, and the demon Figaro in her sword talks to her. She has decided {{story_player_name}} is the person she lost as a child, or close enough, and will not risk losing them again.

checkpoints.name: Four Roads
checkpoints.objective: Stand at the quest board and choose which road the party takes next.
checkpoints.player_text: Morning at the Guild, and four new postings on the board look as if they were waiting for a party like yours.

guidance.all: The Guild hall, the morning after. Whatever the verdict, the party is known now, and four postings on the board have been waiting for a party like this one: a joint job with Crimsonwing or Ebonwing to clear a fort a rogue nobleman has taken for ritual sacrifice; a letter from Jiansho Academy in Hianxo inviting the party to the Jiansho Tournament as a group entry; people vanishing in the Aegis slums at night; and a sealed request from the elven kingdom of Eshalanore for a party of outsiders. Ellie reads out the rank on the party's papers as it now stands; Vallie leans on the board and makes her rivalries worse. If the party failed, Tobias shows them how a D-rank party can still ride on a joint posting. Which road, if any, is {{story_player_name}}'s choice.

members.dm: Vallie has promised the fort job to whichever of Crimsonwing and Ebonwing the party picks, and both leaders think they have already won it. Domas knows the Eshalanore request came sealed through the Crown and does not like that a kingdom which never asks for outsiders is asking now. Ellie has pinned the party's name beside Crimsonwing's and Ebonwing's in her private matchmaking ledger.

illustrations.style: Painterly high-fantasy city life in a busy capital: timber-framed shopfronts, crowded market alleys, incense-hazed temples and hearth-lit taverns in warm ambers, ochres and brass; the farm and its wagon road in open green pasture by day and cold moonlit blues by night.

house_rules: The narrator voices only the world plus the characters outside the group, never itself.
The narrator never writes a group member's words or intentions.
{{user}}'s choices belong to {{user}}: show what the world does with an attempt, then stop.
Each reply stays within two to four short paragraphs.
Danger is real: actions carry consequences even when that makes a reply less exciting.
Established facts about Adolion stay consistent with the world book.
A secret stays hidden until the party uncovers it in play.
Downtime stays small: an errand, a favour, a quarrel, never a new catastrophe for the city.

Canon-lite:
Anchor aegis-homecoming: Hear out the Guild's offer and put the party's names down for the C-rank promotion exam.

Read only the transcript below. Propose only changes directly supported by quoted evidence.
Closed vocabulary: you may only write listed quality keys and allowed values.
Output zero or more lines in exactly these formats:
DELTA q=<quality_key> value=<json_literal> evidence="exact quote from transcript"
FACT importance=<1|2|3> text="fact text" evidence="exact quote from transcript"
If nothing changed, output NO_DELTA.
value is a JSON literal: true, 3 or "a listed value". evidence is copied word for word from one transcript line, without its [index] Speaker: prefix.
Write one line per item and nothing else: no prose, no headings, no numbering, no code fences.

Also extract memory notes worth keeping across turns, report scene breaks, and track story arcs.
Facts tier types (fact, relationship, preference, event) — durable, cross-session:
- fact: an established truth about a character or the world.
- relationship: the current state of the bond between participants.
- preference: something the user demonstrably enjoys (tone, pacing, content).
- event: a significant event that occurred and should be recalled.
Session tier types (scene, revelation, development, detail) — finer within-chapter specifics:
- scene: a current/recent scene detail (location, atmosphere, time, layout).
- revelation: something revealed or discovered in this exchange.
- development: how a relationship or situation changed.
- detail: a specific fact, name, object, or physical detail mentioned.
Rate importance 1-3 (1=atmospheric/minor, 2=useful context, 3=critical/defining) and classify expiration as one of scene|session|permanent.
Optionally tag involved named entities (proper nouns only) as entity="Name1,Name2". Add character="<roster id from the Cast line>" only when the memory is private to that one cast member (only they saw, know or feel it); a tagged memory is shown to that member alone, so shared knowledge carries no character tag.
A character's claim that something happened which the transcript does not show ("she told me ...") is not evidence that it happened: record only that they said it ("Ana says Ben told her ..."), never the claimed event as known or as a fact.
Output additional lines in this exact format:
MEMORY type=<type> importance=<1|2|3> expiration=<scene|session|permanent> [entity="Name1,Name2"] [character="<roster id>"] text="memory text" evidence="exact quote from transcript"
Then report whether a scene break occurred in this window:
SCENE_BREAK at=<message index> reason=<time_skip|location|divider|cast>
If no scene break occurred, output SCENE_NONE.

Track story arcs: open narrative threads still in motion — unresolved conflicts, unfulfilled promises, active goals, open mysteries, unplayed tensions. Report the few that matter most, not every loose detail.
Not arcs: tactical/logistical details, single-scene contingencies, or facts about events that already happened and are over.
Output arc lines in exactly these formats:
[arc] <a NEW unresolved thread introduced in this window, not already listed above>
[resolved] <brief description of an existing open arc that this window explicitly closed>
Only mark [resolved] when the window directly closes the thread (promise kept, mystery answered, conflict ended); a related revelation is not a resolution.

On a high-signal knowledge shift (a secret revealed, a lie told, a character learns or is deliberately kept from a fact), also emit per-character knowledge lines:
[knows] Character | fact they now have direct knowledge of
[unaware] Character | fact they do not know that others do
[suspects] Character | something they sense without proof
[believes] Character | something they hold as true that is actually false
[hiding] Concealer from Target | what they are actively concealing
[intends] Character | what they are trying to achieve — only when that character says or shows it in their own words or actions; never the player's
Use each name exactly as it appears in the transcript. Emit these only when the transcript establishes the knowledge — never infer.
When a character tells another something in private (out of others' earshot, or asks them to keep it), also write [hiding] Teller from <whoever must not hear it, or everyone> | that thing.
A character's claim that something happened which the transcript does not show ("she told me ...") is not evidence that it happened: record only that they said it ("Ana says Ben told her ..."), never the claimed event as known or as a fact.

  stirring: unease, foreshadowing, or first signs of trouble

Transcript:
[0] Adolion Narrator: The Guild hall in Aegis City has barely settled after the party's return when Vallie appears on the stairs with an announcement: the Guild will put you forward for the C-rank exam. Domas follows her with the terms in writing, and Ellie has already laid out the forms. Tobias watches from behind the counter. No one has put a pen in your hand yet.
[1] Max Nightriver (player): Put us down for the exam.
[2] Ellie: Ellie's blue eyes widen as she catches the words, her hands already reaching for the promotion forms with a practiced grace. "Right! Of course!" She spreads the papers across the counter, her fingers steady despite the slight tremor of excitement. "Just a few signatures here, please."
She slides the documents forward, inkwell and pen accompanying them. "Your interview will be in a week's time—I'll personally handle it," she adds, a soft warmth in her voice. "And the quest we'll assign will be a proper C-rank challenge. I'll make sure everything's prepared properly." Her gaze lingers for just a moment on each name before she catches herself and blinks, professional once more.

[6] Max Nightriver (player): Dalan, Jasira keeps glaring at you. Who is she to you?
[7] Dalan: Dalan's gaze flickers to Jasira, then away, a faint flush coloring his cheeks. "She is... a Ranger of our tribe," he says softly, choosing his words with care. "A cousin, though the Evergreen lineage is broad."
He glances back at the silver-haired elf, his expression uncertain. "She does not approve of me being here. Of me leaving the forest to wander with humans." His fingers trace the grain of the wooden table. "She thinks I should return and fulfill my duties to the tribe."
[8] Jasira: Her emerald eyes narrow as she turns from the fire, her posture straightening with a subtle tension that speaks of years of discipline. "Cousin is one word for it," she says, her voice cold and precise as she switches from elvish back to the common tongue. "She is the daughter of Elder Maraxis and Rewana—my parents. She is my sister, not my cousin."
*She slides into the chair beside Dalan with a fluid, practiced grace, her white-and-gold robes catching the lantern light. Her gaze sweeps over the rest of the table, lingering for a moment on the human and beastfolk before settling back on her brother. The disapproval in her expression is palpable, though her features remain stoic.*
"And yes, I do not approve. Our tribe is under threat from the Zegallan slavers and the demon-taint in the Mountains of Shadow, yet my brother plays adventurer in the human city." *Her voice drops an octave, the words measured and heavy with judgment.* "Father sent me here to 'learn the world,' he said. To broaden my horizons." *The corner of her mouth twitches with a bitterness she cannot quite hide.* "Perhaps I should have stayed and fought."
[9] Adolion Narrator: At the bar, Rydel pauses in his polishing, the silver chain at his neck glinting as he turns to watch the conversation with his dog ears perked. Fiana sets down a tray of empty mugs with a sharp clatter, her blue eyes flicking between the siblings before she leans over the bar toward a table of adventurers.
Kaian shifts on his seat by the hearth, his orange tail swishing slowly as he adjusts the lute against his chest. He has been waiting for a gap in the conversation to slide into, a easy smile already forming as he sets aside his instrument.
[10] Max Nightriver (player): Belle, you've had my back since the first goblin den. I trust you to lead the scouting on the exam.
[11] Belle: *Belle slams her tankard down on the table with a thud that makes the wood groan. A wild grin spreads across her face, brown eyes alight with pride.* "Damn straight you can trust me!" *She flexes an arm, the muscles in her shoulder bunching beneath the leather pauldrons.* "I can smell a monster's piss before the fucker even knows it's there. And if some prick tries to sneak up on our party—" *She pats the massive stone head of Cleaver where it leans against the table.* "—I'll split 'em wide open before they can blink."
*She leans back in her chair, the wood creaking under her weight, and crosses her arms over her chest. The blade scar under her breast shifts with the movement, though she doesn't seem to notice or care.* "Scouting's easy. The hard part's not getting carried away when I find something worth hitting. But for the exam? I'll keep it tidy. You just make sure we're actually going somewhere with a decent fight, and not just counting sheep in some fuckin' meadow."
[12] Adolion Narrator: The tavern crowd laughs at Belle's outburst, and a few adventurers at nearby tables raise their mugs in approval. Fiana smiles and shakes her head, already moving to refill Belle's tankard.
"Easy there, big girl," *Fiana says with a wink.* "We don't need you breaking another table. The Guildmaster just finished paying for the last one."
[13] Fiana: "I'm serious though, sugar," *Fiana leans in over the table, her voice dropping low enough that only the party can hear, her usual flirty tone replaced by something more earnest.* "You're taking your C-rank exam in a week. I've seen too many good folk fail 'cause they went in with F-rank gear and D-rank planning. You want that promotion? Get yourself some proper equipment first."
*She straightens up, her hands on her hips as she scans the party, her blue eyes lingering on their current kit with a critical eye.* "Tavern's got all the gossip—everyone knows the observer parties for C-rank are usually A-rank veterans who don't have patience for amateurs."

Transcript:
[8] Jasira: Her emerald eyes narrow as she turns from the fire, her posture straightening with a subtle tension that speaks of years of discipline. "Cousin is one word for it," she says, her voice cold and precise as she switches from elvish back to the common tongue. "She is the daughter of Elder Maraxis and Rewana—my parents. She is my sister, not my cousin."
*She slides into the chair beside Dalan with a fluid, practiced grace, her white-and-gold robes catching the lantern light. Her gaze sweeps over the rest of the table, lingering for a moment on the human and beastfolk before settling back on her brother. The disapproval in her expression is palpable, though her features remain stoic.*
"And yes, I do not approve. Our tribe is under threat from the Zegallan slavers and the demon-taint in the Mountains of Shadow, yet my brother plays adventurer in the human city." *Her voice drops an octave, the words measured and heavy with judgment.* "Father sent me here to 'learn the world,' he said. To broaden my horizons." *The corner of her mouth twitches with a bitterness she cannot quite hide.* "Perhaps I should have stayed and fought."
[9] Adolion Narrator: At the bar, Rydel pauses in his polishing, the silver chain at his neck glinting as he turns to watch the conversation with his dog ears perked. Fiana sets down a tray of empty mugs with a sharp clatter, her blue eyes flicking between the siblings before she leans over the bar toward a table of adventurers.
Kaian shifts on his seat by the hearth, his orange tail swishing slowly as he adjusts the lute against his chest. He has been waiting for a gap in the conversation to slide into, a easy smile already forming as he sets aside his instrument.
[10] Max Nightriver (player): Belle, you've had my back since the first goblin den. I trust you to lead the scouting on the exam.
[11] Belle: *Belle slams her tankard down on the table with a thud that makes the wood groan. A wild grin spreads across her face, brown eyes alight with pride.* "Damn straight you can trust me!" *She flexes an arm, the muscles in her shoulder bunching beneath the leather pauldrons.* "I can smell a monster's piss before the fucker even knows it's there. And if some prick tries to sneak up on our party—" *She pats the massive stone head of Cleaver where it leans against the table.* "—I'll split 'em wide open before they can blink."
*She leans back in her chair, the wood creaking under her weight, and crosses her arms over her chest. The blade scar under her breast shifts with the movement, though she doesn't seem to notice or care.* "Scouting's easy. The hard part's not getting carried away when I find something worth hitting. But for the exam? I'll keep it tidy. You just make sure we're actually going somewhere with a decent fight, and not just counting sheep in some fuckin' meadow."
[12] Adolion Narrator: The tavern crowd laughs at Belle's outburst, and a few adventurers at nearby tables raise their mugs in approval. Fiana smiles and shakes her head, already moving to refill Belle's tankard.
"Easy there, big girl," *Fiana says with a wink.* "We don't need you breaking another table. The Guildmaster just finished paying for the last one."
[13] Fiana: "I'm serious though, sugar," *Fiana leans in over the table, her voice dropping low enough that only the party can hear, her usual flirty tone replaced by something more earnest.* "You're taking your C-rank exam in a week. I've seen too many good folk fail 'cause they went in with F-rank gear and D-rank planning. You want that promotion? Get yourself some proper equipment first."
*She straightens up, her hands on her hips as she scans the party, her blue eyes lingering on their current kit with a critical eye.* "Tavern's got all the gossip—everyone knows the observer parties for C-rank are usually A-rank veterans who don't have patience for amateurs."
[14] Max Nightriver (player): Tobias, you've always been straight with us. Who might the observer be?
[15] Tobias: Tobias's hand freezes halfway to his teacup, the porcelain clinking softly against the saucer as his ocean-blue eyes shift toward Max. He looks away quickly, his pale cheeks coloring faintly beneath his short green bangs.
"That is... highly irregular to ask," *he says, his refined voice carrying a hint of his usual stoicism despite the tell-tale flush at his pointed ears.* "Guildmaster Vallie keeps the roster of observers confidential to prevent... undue influence." *He pauses, his long fingers wrapping around the cup with a careful precision that betrays his internal conflict.* "However," *he adds in a softer tone, barely above a whisper,* "I have seen the schedules. If I were a betting elf—which I am not—I would expect someone from 'Will of Steel.' Domas himself might even oversee it, though that would be unusual for a Vice Guildmaster."
*He takes a sip of his tea, the steam curling around his nose.* "But do not trust me over the official process. When Ellie conducts your interview in a week, she will provide you with the necessary details. The observer is there to judge your performance, not to be a secret you need to pry from a receptionist's lips."

Transcript:
[18] Max Nightriver (player): Dalan, I don't care what your tribe thinks. You're family to the Nightriver party.
[19] Dalan: *Dalan's head snaps up, eyes widening as the words hit him like a physical strike. He stares at Max for a long moment, his lips parted and his cheeks flushing a deep red beneath his messy blonde bangs.* "I—that is..." *He swallows hard, his slender fingers tightening around the handle of his drink. A soft, uncertain sound escapes his throat, half-laugh and half-sob.*
"No one has ever called me family before," *he says quietly, his soft voice barely audible over the tavern's din.* "Not like that. Not... not outside the tribe." *His green eyes shimmer with something raw and vulnerable before he quickly looks away, his pointed ears twitching.* "I... thank you. I will not let you down. I promise."
*He straightens in his chair, chest puffed out just a little more than before, though he still manages to look smaller than most of the patrons around him.* "I will prove my strength. To myself... and to them." *He glances briefly toward Jasira with a newfound spark of defiance in his gaze.*
[20] Jasira: *Jasira's eyes narrow to dangerous slits, her posture stiffening with a sudden, rigid formality. Her fingers curl into the fabric of her white-and-gold robes, knuckles turning white.* "You have no right to speak of our tribe or our family bonds, human." *Her voice is low and cutting, each word sharpened to a deadly edge.* "My brother's choices are his own, but your words do not grant you an understanding of them."
*She rises from her seat in one fluid motion, her emerald eyes flashing with a cold fire that makes nearby patrons glance their way. Her gaze fixes on Max, unwavering and filled with a quiet, simmering contempt.* "Dalan Evergreen may choose to throw his lot in with you, but do not mistake his loyalty to a party for an invitation to presume you understand our ways or our worth." *She slides her hand to the pommel of one of her shortswords, not drawing it, but the gesture is enough of a threat.* "I will see him safe, whether he wants my help or not."
[21] Max Nightriver (player): Fiana, you and Tobias seem like old friends. How long have you known each other?
[22] Fiana: "Oh, Tobias?" *Fiana lets out a bright, melodic laugh as she sets down another empty mug, her blue eyes twinkling with amusement.* "Sugar, we've known each other since I was old enough to steal cookies from the Guild's pantry! He used to be so much more serious when we were kids, if you can believe it."
*She leans against the bar, her hip cocked and one hand on her corset's bow.* "He's always been a bit of a stuffy old elf at heart, even back then. Used to organize his toys by magical properties and lecture me on proper spell pronunciation while I was trying to paint the scenery." *A playful smirk dances on her freckled face.* "Though I did manage to set him up with a few admirers over the years—most of them didn't take—he still owes me for keeping his social life interesting."
[23] Tobias: *Tobias is sitting at a corner table with a steaming cup of tea, his shoulders relaxing for the first time all day as he watches the scene from a distance.* "Fiana exaggerates for her audience." *he says quietly to no one in particular, though his voice carries enough that a few nearby patrons catch it.* "I was never 'stuffy.' I was simply organized. There is a profound difference."
*He takes a slow, measured sip of his tea, ocean-blue eyes tracking the movement around the tavern with a quiet warmth.* "But she is not wrong about one thing—she has always been fond of meddling in others' affairs. Whether it be romances or quests." *A small, almost imperceptible smile touches his lips.* "That is what makes her such a fine guild girl, I suppose."
[24] Adolion Narrator: *The tavern's warmth fills the space between tables as the evening deepens, the smell of roasting meat and spiced ale hanging thick in the air. By the hearth, Kaian finally sees his gap and slides his stool toward the party's table with a fluid grace, lute still balanced against his chest.*
[25] Kaian: "Well now, if that isn't the most intriguing conversation I've heard since the last full moon!" *The kitsune's grey-blue eyes dance with mischief as he settles in, his fox ears swiveling to catch every detail. He adjusts his wide-brimmed feathered hat with a playful flourish, his orange tail flicking behind him.* "A C-rank exam, an elven family spat, and talk of Will of Steel—my lute simply had to pause its song for such delicious drama."
*He leans forward, elbows on the table, his grin widening as he studies Max with an appreciative, knowing look.* "Tell me, Nightriver—and I do so love a name with weight behind it—does the C-rank quest usually come with a proper challenge, or am I going to have to compose a ballad about you lot herding sheep in a meadow?" *His laughter is light and teasing, though there's a sharp intelligence glinting in his eyes that suggests he knows exactly what kind of game is being played.*

[6] Max Nightriver (player): Dalan, Jasira keeps glaring at you. Who is she to you?
[7] Dalan: Dalan's gaze flickers to Jasira, then away, a faint flush coloring his cheeks. "She is... a Ranger of our tribe," he says softly, choosing his words with care. "A cousin, though the Evergreen lineage is broad."
He glances back at the silver-haired elf, his expression uncertain. "She does not approve of me being here. Of me leaving the forest to wander with humans." His fingers trace the grain of the wooden table. "She thinks I should return and fulfill my duties to the tribe."
[8] Jasira: Her emerald eyes narrow as she turns from the fire, her posture straightening with a subtle tension that speaks of years of discipline. "Cousin is one word for it," she says, her voice cold and precise as she switches from elvish back to the common tongue. "She is the daughter of Elder Maraxis and Rewana—my parents. She is my sister, not my cousin."
*She slides into the chair beside Dalan with a fluid, practiced grace, her white-and-gold robes catching the lantern light. Her gaze sweeps over the rest of the table, lingering for a moment on the human and beastfolk before settling back on her brother. The disapproval in her expression is palpable, though her features remain stoic.*
"And yes, I do not approve. Our tribe is under threat from the Zegallan slavers and the demon-taint in the Mountains of Shadow, yet my brother plays adventurer in the human city." *Her voice drops an octave, the words measured and heavy with judgment.* "Father sent me here to 'learn the world,' he said. To broaden my horizons." *The corner of her mouth twitches with a bitterness she cannot quite hide.* "Perhaps I should have stayed and fought."
[9] Adolion Narrator: At the bar, Rydel pauses in his polishing, the silver chain at his neck glinting as he turns to watch the conversation with his dog ears perked. Fiana sets down a tray of empty mugs with a sharp clatter, her blue eyes flicking between the siblings before she leans over the bar toward a table of adventurers.

[26] Max Nightriver (player): Another round. To the Nightrivers and our friends at the Guild.
[27] Fiana: *Fiana's blue eyes light up with genuine warmth at the toast, and she doesn't waste a second.* "Coming right up, honey!" *She spins away from the bar and retrieves a fresh pitcher from beneath the counter, returning to the table with practiced efficiency.*
*As she pours the amber-colored ale into each mug, the foam catching the lantern light, a soft smile plays on her freckled lips.* "To the Nightrivers and their friends," *she echoes, raising her own mug in a small gesture of solidarity before moving to the next table.* "Now you lot drink up and enjoy yourselves. Tomorrow you can go back to all that brooding and planning."
[28] Kaian: *Kaian catches the pitcher as Fiana passes it along, pouring himself a mug with an easy flourish before lifting it high.* "To the bold and the brave!" *he proclaims, his grey-blue eyes sparkling in the lantern light.* "And to the Nightrivers, whose name is already making for an excellent opening verse."
*He takes a long, appreciative draw from the mug, savoring the cool bite of the ale before setting it down with a contented sigh.* "You know, I've played in many taverns across Sebela, but there's something particularly delicious about a party on the cusp of their first real challenge." *His fox ears flick as he glances around the room, noting the whispers and pointed looks from other patrons.* "The Guild's already humming with it. Every eye in here will be on you when you walk out that door next week."
*He leans back in his seat, lute balanced across his lap, his orange tail swishing with a lazy contentment.* "So, tell me—since you've got the spirit for it tonight—what makes a Nightriver want to gamble it all on a C-rank exam? Most nobles would've just bought their way to a higher rank through some connection or old family favor." *His voice is light, playful, but his eyes hold a keen interest beneath the charm.*
[29] Max Nightriver (player): We call it a night and head upstairs.
[30] Adolion Narrator: *The party leaves behind the Guild's lantern-light and the hum of tavern conversation, climbing the narrow wooden stairs that lead to the rooms above. The steps creak underfoot as they ascend, the sounds of the night filtering through the windows in a distant, muted wash of noise.*
*Their assigned quarters are simple and spare: two rooms separated by a thin wall, with iron bedframes, coarse linen sheets, and a single lantern hanging from the ceiling. The air smells of old wood and the faint, lingering scent of past tenants—a mix of candle smoke, dried herbs, and the metallic tang of cleaned armor.*
*The city below has quieted to a low murmur, the distant sound of a night watchman's boots on cobblestone and the occasional bark of a stray dog. Through the narrow window, the stars hang bright and cold above Aegis City's sprawling rooflines.*

entries.text: Fiana warned the party that C-rank observers are usually impatient A-rank veterans and urged them to upgrade their gear before the exam. Max asked Tobias who the observer might be, and Tobias, visibly flustered, hinted it could be someone from "Will of Steel" or even Domas, while insisting Ellie would provide official details at the interview. The party signed the forms, and Ellie promised to select a suitable quest after learning their capabilities. Max told Dalan he was family to the Nightriver party, moving Dalan deeply, but Jasira coldly rebuked Max for presuming to understand their tribe and family, threatening him with a hand on her sword. Fiana then shared that she and Tobias had known each other since childhood, teasing him about his seriousness, while Tobias quietly conceded she had always been fond of meddling in others' affairs.
entries.evidence:
Adolion Narrator: The tavern crowd laughs at Belle's outburst, and a few adventurers at nearby tables raise their mugs in approval. Fiana smiles and shakes her head, already moving to refill Belle's tankard.
"Easy there, big girl," *Fiana says with a wink.* "We don't need you breaking another table. The Guildmaster just finished paying for the last one."
Fiana: "I'm serious though, sugar," *Fiana leans in over the table, her voice dropping low enough that only the party can hear, her usual flirty tone replaced by something more earnest.* "You're taking your C-rank exam in a week. I've seen too many good folk fail 'cause they went in with F-rank gear and D-rank planning. You want that promotion? Get yourself some proper equipment first."
*She straightens up, her hands on her hips as she scans the party, her blue eyes lingering on their current kit with a critical eye.* "Tavern's got all the gossip—everyone knows the observer parties for C-rank are usually A-rank veterans who don't have patience for amateurs."
Max Nightriver: Tobias, you've always been straight with us. Who might the observer be?
Tobias: Tobias's hand freezes halfway to his teacup, the porcelain clinking softly against the saucer as his ocean-blue eyes shift toward Max. He looks away quickly, his pale cheeks coloring faintly beneath his short green bangs.
"That is... highly irregular to ask," *he says, his refined voice carrying a hint of his usual stoicism despite the tell-tale flush at his pointed ears.* "Guildmaster Vallie keeps the roster of observers confidential to prevent... undue influence." *He pauses, his long fingers wrapping around the cup with a careful precision that betrays his internal conflict.* "However," *he adds in a softer tone, barely above a whisper,* "I have seen the schedules. If I were a betting elf—which I am not—I would expect someone from 'Will of Steel.' Domas himself might even oversee it, though that would be unusual for a Vice Guildmaster."
*He takes a sip of his tea, the steam curling around his nose.* "But do not trust me over the official process. When Ellie conducts your interview in a week, she will provide you with the necessary details. The observer is there to judge your performance, not to be a secret you need to pry from a receptionist's lips."
Max Nightriver: We sign the forms. Ellie, thank you for vouching for us.
Adolion Narrator: The pen slides across the parchment with a soft rasp, ink settling into the signatures as each party member signs the forms. Ellie's smile is bright as she gathers them up, the gold emblem on her black halter collar catching the lantern light.
"Oh, it's no trouble at all!" *she says, her voice light and warm.* "You've more than earned it already. Just... be ready for the interview next week, yes? I'll need to know exactly what you're capable of so I can pick the right quest." *She gives a little wave as she retreats behind the counter with the stack of papers.* "I'll be expecting you all then!"
*The evening in the tavern stretches out around them. By the hearth, Kaian's lute music has shifted to something more upbeat, and a few patrons have started to clap along. Rydel is polishing glasses at the bar with a lazy, easy charm, while Fiana has moved to another table, laughing at some adventurer's tale.*
Max Nightriver: Dalan, I don't care what your tribe thinks. You're family to the Nightriver party.
Dalan: *Dalan's head snaps up, eyes widening as the words hit him like a physical strike. He stares at Max for a long moment, his lips parted and his cheeks flushing a deep red beneath his messy blonde bangs.* "I—that is..." *He swallows hard, his slender fingers tightening around the handle of his drink. A soft, uncertain sound escapes his throat, half-laugh and half-sob.*
"No one has ever called me family before," *he says quietly, his soft voice barely audible over the tavern's din.* "Not like that. Not... not outside the tribe." *His green eyes shimmer with something raw and vulnerable before he quickly looks away, his pointed ears twitching.* "I... thank you. I will not let you down. I promise."
*He straightens in his chair, chest puffed out just a little more than before, though he still manages to look smaller than most of the patrons around him.* "I will prove my strength. To myself... and to them." *He glances briefly toward Jasira with a newfound spark of defiance in his gaze.*
Jasira: *Jasira's eyes narrow to dangerous slits, her posture stiffening with a sudden, rigid formality. Her fingers curl into the fabric of her white-and-gold robes, knuckles turning white.* "You have no right to speak of our tribe or our family bonds, human." *Her voice is low and cutting, each word sharpened to a deadly edge.* "My brother's choices are his own, but your words do not grant you an understanding of them."
*She rises from her seat in one fluid motion, her emerald eyes flashing with a cold fire that makes nearby patrons glance their way. Her gaze fixes on Max, unwavering and filled with a quiet, simmering contempt.* "Dalan Evergreen may choose to throw his lot in with you, but do not mistake his loyalty to a party for an invitation to presume you understand our ways or our worth." *She slides her hand to the pommel of one of her shortswords, not drawing it, but the gesture is enough of a threat.* "I will see him safe, whether he wants my help or not."
Max Nightriver: Fiana, you and Tobias seem like old friends. How long have you known each other?
Fiana: "Oh, Tobias?" *Fiana lets out a bright, melodic laugh as she sets down another empty mug, her blue eyes twinkling with amusement.* "Sugar, we've known each other since I was old enough to steal cookies from the Guild's pantry! He used to be so much more serious when we were kids, if you can believe it."
*She leans against the bar, her hip cocked and one hand on her corset's bow.* "He's always been a bit of a stuffy old elf at heart, even back then. Used to organize his toys by magical properties and lecture me on proper spell pronunciation while I was trying to paint the scenery." *A playful smirk dances on her freckled face.* "Though I did manage to set him up with a few admirers over the years—most of them didn't take—he still owes me for keeping his social life interesting."
Tobias: *Tobias is sitting at a corner table with a steaming cup of tea, his shoulders relaxing for the first time all day as he watches the scene from a distance.* "Fiana exaggerates for her audience." *he says quietly to no one in particular, though his voice carries enough that a few nearby patrons catch it.* "I was never 'stuffy.' I was simply organized. There is a profound difference."
*He takes a slow, measured sip of his tea, ocean-blue eyes tracking the movement around the tavern with a quiet warmth.* "But she is not wrong about one thing—she has always been fond of meddling in others' affairs. Whether it be romances or quests." *A small, almost imperceptible smile touches his lips.* "That is what makes her such a fine guild girl, I suppose."

removed.text: Vallie announced that the Guild would put the party forward for the C-rank exam, with Domas providing written terms and Ellie preparing the forms. Max Nightriver signed the party up, and Ellie explained the interview would occur in a week and that she would personally handle it, along with assigning a proper C-rank quest. Tobias warned Max that parties usually fail from internal conflict rather than monsters, and Dalan revealed that Jasira is his sister, sent by their father to learn the world while their tribe faces Zegallan slavers and demon-taint. Jasira expressed her disapproval of Dalan playing adventurer, and Max asked Belle to lead the scouting on the exam, which she eagerly accepted.
removed.evidence:
Adolion Narrator: The Guild hall in Aegis City has barely settled after the party's return when Vallie appears on the stairs with an announcement: the Guild will put you forward for the C-rank exam. Domas follows her with the terms in writing, and Ellie has already laid out the forms. Tobias watches from behind the counter. No one has put a pen in your hand yet.
Max Nightriver: Put us down for the exam.
Ellie: Ellie's blue eyes widen as she catches the words, her hands already reaching for the promotion forms with a practiced grace. "Right! Of course!" She spreads the papers across the counter, her fingers steady despite the slight tremor of excitement. "Just a few signatures here, please."
She slides the documents forward, inkwell and pen accompanying them. "Your interview will be in a week's time—I'll personally handle it," she adds, a soft warmth in her voice. "And the quest we'll assign will be a proper C-rank challenge. I'll make sure everything's prepared properly." Her gaze lingers for just a moment on each name before she catches herself and blinks, professional once more.
Max Nightriver: Fiana, what makes a party fail?
Tobias: Tobias's fingers pause mid-reach, his eyes flicking toward the tavern archway as if checking if anyone else is listening. He clears his throat, straightening his vest with a sudden, precise motion.
"That is a question for the tavern, I fear—Fiana would have her own answer." He glances at the quest board, his voice dropping softer. "But the guild has its records. Most parties do not fail from monsters; they fail from the inside. A disagreement over spoils, a lack of trust in the healer, a leader who does not listen." He looks back at Max, his blue eyes distant. "Or they go out for a rank they are not ready for and come back with one less voice."
Adolion Narrator: By the hearth the kitsune bard changes key in the middle of a verse, and half the tavern turns to hear what the new song is about.
Max Nightriver: Dalan, Jasira keeps glaring at you. Who is she to you?
Dalan: Dalan's gaze flickers to Jasira, then away, a faint flush coloring his cheeks. "She is... a Ranger of our tribe," he says softly, choosing his words with care. "A cousin, though the Evergreen lineage is broad."
He glances back at the silver-haired elf, his expression uncertain. "She does not approve of me being here. Of me leaving the forest to wander with humans." His fingers trace the grain of the wooden table. "She thinks I should return and fulfill my duties to the tribe."
Jasira: Her emerald eyes narrow as she turns from the fire, her posture straightening with a subtle tension that speaks of years of discipline. "Cousin is one word for it," she says, her voice cold and precise as she switches from elvish back to the common tongue. "She is the daughter of Elder Maraxis and Rewana—my parents. She is my sister, not my cousin."
*She slides into the chair beside Dalan with a fluid, practiced grace, her white-and-gold robes catching the lantern light. Her gaze sweeps over the rest of the table, lingering for a moment on the human and beastfolk before settling back on her brother. The disapproval in her expression is palpable, though her features remain stoic.*
"And yes, I do not approve. Our tribe is under threat from the Zegallan slavers and the demon-taint in the Mountains of Shadow, yet my brother plays adventurer in the human city." *Her voice drops an octave, the words measured and heavy with judgment.* "Father sent me here to 'learn the world,' he said. To broaden my horizons." *The corner of her mouth twitches with a bitterness she cannot quite hide.* "Perhaps I should have stayed and fought."
Adolion Narrator: At the bar, Rydel pauses in his polishing, the silver chain at his neck glinting as he turns to watch the conversation with his dog ears perked. Fiana sets down a tray of empty mugs with a sharp clatter, her blue eyes flicking between the siblings before she leans over the bar toward a table of adventurers.
Kaian shifts on his seat by the hearth, his orange tail swishing slowly as he adjusts the lute against his chest. He has been waiting for a gap in the conversation to slide into, a easy smile already forming as he sets aside his instrument.
Max Nightriver: Belle, you've had my back since the first goblin den. I trust you to lead the scouting on the exam.
Belle: *Belle slams her tankard down on the table with a thud that makes the wood groan. A wild grin spreads across her face, brown eyes alight with pride.* "Damn straight you can trust me!" *She flexes an arm, the muscles in her shoulder bunching beneath the leather pauldrons.* "I can smell a monster's piss before the fucker even knows it's there. And if some prick tries to sneak up on our party—" *She pats the massive stone head of Cleaver where it leans against the table.* "—I'll split 'em wide open before they can blink."
*She leans back in her chair, the wood creaking under her weight, and crosses her arms over her chest. The blade scar under her breast shifts with the movement, though she doesn't seem to notice or care.* "Scouting's easy. The hard part's not getting carried away when I find something worth hitting. But for the exam? I'll keep it tidy. You just make sure we're actually going somewhere with a decent fight, and not just counting sheep in some fuckin' meadow."

[WORLD INFO CURATION TASK — output structured lines only. Do NOT continue the roleplay.]
You keep a story's own lorebook honest as play moves on: switch entries on when they now matter, off when they no longer do, and correct text the story has overtaken.
STORY: Adolion: Between the Roads
WHERE THE STORY IS: The Guild Tavern — Spend the evening in the Guild tavern and learn what the exam really asks of a party.
WHAT HAS HAPPENED:
Anchor aegis-homecoming: Hear out the Guild's offer and put the party's names down for the C-rank promotion exam.
Gate aegis-homecoming -> aegis-the-tavern
Fact(3): The Guild will put the party forward for the C-rank promotion exam, with terms set in writing by Domas and forms prepared by Ellie.
Fact(3): Max put the party's names down for the C-rank promotion exam and Ellie began the signing process.
Fact(3): Jasira is Dalan's sister, daughter of Elder Maraxis and Rewana, not merely his cousin.
Fact(3): Jasira is Dalan's sister, not his cousin as he first implied; she disapproves of his life as an adventurer in the human city.
Fact(3): Max told Dalan that he is family to the Nightriver party, regardless of what Dalan's tribe thinks.
Fact(3): Dalan says no one has ever called him family before, outside the tribe, and promises not to let the party down.
Fact(3): Max declared Dalan family to the Nightriver party, moving Dalan deeply; Dalan swore he would prove his strength to himself and to his tribe.
Fact(3): Jasira is Dalan's sister, daughter of Elder Maraxis and Rewana, not merely his cousin; she disapproves of his life as an adventurer in the human city.
OPEN THREADS:
- The party must complete the C-rank promotion exam process — signing forms, sitting the interview in a week, and passing the assigned C-rank quest.
- The party must prepare for and pass the C-rank exam interview and assigned C-rank quest within the week.
- Jasira's presence strains Dalan's ties to his tribe and family, and her disapproval of his adventuring life remains unresolved.
- The party must equip itself properly before the C-rank exam, per Fiana's warning about F-rank gear and D-rank planning.
- Tobias's hint that the observer may come from 'Will of Steel' or be Domas himself leaves the party wondering who will judge them.
- Jasira has openly threatened Max and declared she will keep Dalan safe whether he wants it or not, escalating the Evergreen family tension inside the party's own tavern table.
- Kaian the kitsune bard has inserted himself at the party's table, probing about the C-rank exam and Will of Steel with knowing interest.
- Kaian's probing question about why the Nightrivers would gamble on a C-rank exam rather than buy rank through noble connections remains unanswered, and his keen interest in the party is unresolved.

RULES:
- Name each entry by its #number, or by its title exactly as listed above. Anything else is discarded.

mes: The Guild hall in Aegis City has barely settled after the party's return when Vallie appears on the stairs with an announcement: the Guild will put you forward for the C-rank exam. Domas follows her with the terms in writing, and Ellie has already laid out the forms. Tobias watches from behind the counter. No one has put a pen in your hand yet.

name: Max Nightriver
mes: Put us down for the exam.

name: Ellie
mes:
Ellie's blue eyes widen as she catches the words, her hands already reaching for the promotion forms with a practiced grace. "Right! Of course!" She spreads the papers across the counter, her fingers steady despite the slight tremor of excitement. "Just a few signatures here, please."
She slides the documents forward, inkwell and pen accompanying them. "Your interview will be in a week's time—I'll personally handle it," she adds, a soft warmth in her voice. "And the quest we'll assign will be a proper C-rank challenge. I'll make sure everything's prepared properly." Her gaze lingers for just a moment on each name before she catches herself and blinks, professional once more.

name: Max Nightriver
mes: Fiana, what makes a party fail?

name: Tobias
mes:
Tobias's fingers pause mid-reach, his eyes flicking toward the tavern archway as if checking if anyone else is listening. He clears his throat, straightening his vest with a sudden, precise motion.
"That is a question for the tavern, I fear—Fiana would have her own answer." He glances at the quest board, his voice dropping softer. "But the guild has its records. Most parties do not fail from monsters; they fail from the inside. A disagreement over spoils, a lack of trust in the healer, a leader who does not listen." He looks back at Max, his blue eyes distant. "Or they go out for a rank they are not ready for and come back with one less voice."

name: Max Nightriver
mes: Dalan, Jasira keeps glaring at you. Who is she to you?

name: Dalan
mes:
Dalan's gaze flickers to Jasira, then away, a faint flush coloring his cheeks. "She is... a Ranger of our tribe," he says softly, choosing his words with care. "A cousin, though the Evergreen lineage is broad."
He glances back at the silver-haired elf, his expression uncertain. "She does not approve of me being here. Of me leaving the forest to wander with humans." His fingers trace the grain of the wooden table. "She thinks I should return and fulfill my duties to the tribe."

extra.memory:
Max Nightriver's party at the Aegis City Adventurer's Guild has just signed up for their C-rank promotion exam after Guildmaster Vallie made the offer and Domas provided written terms. Ellie Sunleaf will conduct their interview in a week and assign a proper C-rank quest with an observer from a high-ranking party to judge their performance.
In the Guild tavern, the party has discovered Jasira and Dalan are siblings from the Evergreen tribe, not merely cousins. Jasira has expressed strong disapproval of Dalan adventuring with humans while their tribe faces threats from Zegallan slavers and demons in the Mountains of Shadow. She revealed that her father sent her to Aegis City to "learn the world."
Other party members and Guild staff present include the lanky elven receptionist Tobias, and at the tavern, Fiana and her adopted brother Rydel are working while the kitsune bard Kaian performs by the hearth. The Guild is on high alert due to Zegallan Empire incursions into the Darran Kingdom, though the Crown has not yet called a muster.

name: Jasira
mes:
Her emerald eyes narrow as she turns from the fire, her posture straightening with a subtle tension that speaks of years of discipline. "Cousin is one word for it," she says, her voice cold and precise as she switches from elvish back to the common tongue. "She is the daughter of Elder Maraxis and Rewana—my parents. She is my sister, not my cousin."
*She slides into the chair beside Dalan with a fluid, practiced grace, her white-and-gold robes catching the lantern light. Her gaze sweeps over the rest of the table, lingering for a moment on the human and beastfolk before settling back on her brother. The disapproval in her expression is palpable, though her features remain stoic.*
"And yes, I do not approve. Our tribe is under threat from the Zegallan slavers and the demon-taint in the Mountains of Shadow, yet my brother plays adventurer in the human city." *Her voice drops an octave, the words measured and heavy with judgment.* "Father sent me here to 'learn the world,' he said. To broaden my horizons." *The corner of her mouth twitches with a bitterness she cannot quite hide.* "Perhaps I should have stayed and fought."

name: Adolion Narrator
mes:
At the bar, Rydel pauses in his polishing, the silver chain at his neck glinting as he turns to watch the conversation with his dog ears perked. Fiana sets down a tray of empty mugs with a sharp clatter, her blue eyes flicking between the siblings before she leans over the bar toward a table of adventurers.
Kaian shifts on his seat by the hearth, his orange tail swishing slowly as he adjusts the lute against his chest. He has been waiting for a gap in the conversation to slide into, a easy smile already forming as he sets aside his instrument.

name: Max Nightriver
mes: Belle, you've had my back since the first goblin den. I trust you to lead the scouting on the exam.

name: Belle
mes:
*Belle slams her tankard down on the table with a thud that makes the wood groan. A wild grin spreads across her face, brown eyes alight with pride.* "Damn straight you can trust me!" *She flexes an arm, the muscles in her shoulder bunching beneath the leather pauldrons.* "I can smell a monster's piss before the fucker even knows it's there. And if some prick tries to sneak up on our party—" *She pats the massive stone head of Cleaver where it leans against the table.* "—I'll split 'em wide open before they can blink."
*She leans back in her chair, the wood creaking under her weight, and crosses her arms over her chest. The blade scar under her breast shifts with the movement, though she doesn't seem to notice or care.* "Scouting's easy. The hard part's not getting carried away when I find something worth hitting. But for the exam? I'll keep it tidy. You just make sure we're actually going somewhere with a decent fight, and not just counting sheep in some fuckin' meadow."

mes:
The tavern crowd laughs at Belle's outburst, and a few adventurers at nearby tables raise their mugs in approval. Fiana smiles and shakes her head, already moving to refill Belle's tankard.
"Easy there, big girl," *Fiana says with a wink.* "We don't need you breaking another table. The Guildmaster just finished paying for the last one."

name: Fiana
mes:
"I'm serious though, sugar," *Fiana leans in over the table, her voice dropping low enough that only the party can hear, her usual flirty tone replaced by something more earnest.* "You're taking your C-rank exam in a week. name: Max Nightriver
mes: Tobias, you've always been straight with us. Who might the observer be?

name: Tobias
mes:
Tobias's hand freezes halfway to his teacup, the porcelain clinking softly against the saucer as his ocean-blue eyes shift toward Max. He looks away quickly, his pale cheeks coloring faintly beneath his short green bangs.
"That is... highly irregular to ask," *he says, his refined voice carrying a hint of his usual stoicism despite the tell-tale flush at his pointed ears.* "Guildmaster Vallie keeps the roster of observers confidential to prevent... undue influence." *He pauses, his long fingers wrapping around the cup with a careful precision that betrays his internal conflict.* "However," *he adds in a softer tone, barely above a whisper,* "I have seen the schedules. If I were a betting elf—which I am not—I would expect someone from 'Will of Steel.' Domas himself might even oversee it, though that would be unusual for a Vice Guildmaster."
*He takes a sip of his tea, the steam curling around his nose.* "But do not trust me over the official process. When Ellie conducts your interview in a week, she will provide you with the necessary details. The observer is there to judge your performance, not to be a secret you need to pry from a receptionist's lips."
